questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle improperly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You lose extra points on your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If you are driving a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will cause you to fail the entire test.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching a school bus stop?

options.text: Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: What should be done if a school bus gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should get off near the bus.
Students should be evacuated and moved far away from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should be evacuated and moved far away from the bus.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone immediately. Move students far away from the bus at an angle away from any oncoming train to avoid debris from a collision.

questions.question: What happens if your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing?

options.text: You do not need to do anything about railroad crossings.
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your driving test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would properly cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: What must happen if there is a fire on a school bus?

options.text: Students should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
Students should remain in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students must be evacuated.
questions.explanation: If there is a fire or risk of fire on a school bus, the driver must evacuate all students immediately.

questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be part of a post-trip bus inspection?

options.text: Looking for articles left on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening windows.
questions.explanation: A post-trip inspection should include checking for sleeping students, belongings left on the bus, open windows or doors, any mechanical problems, and signs of damage. Opening windows is not part of the inspection.

questions.question: What can you NOT see with properly adjusted crossover mirrors?

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors show the entire area in front of the bus and the right and left front tires on the ground. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip check, what should you look for?

options.text: A gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a tractor/trailer coupling, check the fifth wheel gap to make sure the locking jaws are completely closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: Is backing a school bus recommended?

options.text: Yes, but only in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged and should only be done if there is no safe alternative. If you must back up, follow all proper safety steps.

questions.question: If a tornado is coming and there is no shelter nearby, where should students go?
questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby ditch
questions.explanation: If a tornado is sighted and the bus is in danger, the driver should take students to shelter in a building. If no building is available, go to a ditch or culvert. Stay away from areas with flood risk and far enough from the bus so it cannot fall on them.

questions.question: A roof-mounted strobe light should be used:
questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot see well.
questions.explanation: Use the roof-mounted strobe light when visibility is poor.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the passengers.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror helps you watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should check that:

options.text: The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing blocks the pedals and they work properly. Make sure the pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students die during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety rules during these times.

questions.question: For driver's side parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Go forward directly into the space.
Back up past the space, then go forward into it.
Go forward past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your left. Then back up into the space, getting as close to the rear as possible. Your vehicle must be fully inside the boundaries.

questions.question: Except for straight line backing, a driver can exit and check the vehicle's position up to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can get out to check your position up to two times during most tests. For straight line backing, you can only check once.

questions.question: After students leave at school, the driver should:

options.text: Not worry about where students go.
Leave after students enter the building.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students leave, walk through the bus to check for sleeping students, hiding students, and items left behind.

questions.question: When getting on a school bus, students should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Form a single line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single line. They should hold the handrail for safety.

questions.question: If a student drops something while approaching the bus, they should:

options.text: Have another student pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to get a dropped item, the driver cannot see them. This is dangerous. Students should move to a safe spot, get the driver's attention, and let the driver retrieve the item.
